data.question: Which named people and organizations create multiple documented paths among WEF, Trump, Vance, Fink, BlackRock and Palantir?
data.method: Primary/first-party reconciliation against canonical StarIntel records; Reuters retained only as secondary evidence for Rockbridge.
data.framework: Separate WEF status, appointment, employment, founding, investment, event participation and donor-network reporting.
findings: Kratsios is documented as a 2020 WEF Young Global Leader, Trump technology-policy official and former Thiel Capital Principal.
Sacks is documented as a WEF Annual Meeting 2026 speaker and PCAST co-chair; his PayPal-network path exists elsewhere in the corpus.
Existing records connect Helberg to Palantir/Alex Karp and State; the White House placed him in the 2026 India AI delegation led by Kratsios.
Founders Fund identifies Stephens as partner, Anduril co-founder/executive chairman and former early Palantir employee.
8VC identifies Lonsdale as founder/managing partner, Palantir founder and early Anduril investor.
Reuters reports Vance co-founded Rockbridge and Thiel was among its backers; this remains secondary evidence.
The first announced 2026 PCAST member set was co-chaired by Kratsios and Sacks and did not name a Palantir executive, Stephens or Lonsdale.
conclusions: Kratsios is the strongest resolved WEF–Trump–Thiel personnel crossover in this depth.
Sacks is a second WEF-event–White-House crossover.
Helberg, Stephens and Lonsdale resolve distinct Palantir-side bridges.
Overlap does not establish common control, covert coordination, policy capture or misconduct.
recommendations: Run depth 2 for Rockbridge/PCAST primary records and official WEF cross-matches.
counterarguments: WEF participation is not governance; employment or investment does not establish direction or policy control.
limitations: No direct WEF role was established here for Helberg, Stephens or Lonsdale; Rockbridge evidence is secondary.
